headline: The semis ETF fell 7.0% in a day and is down 14.2% on the month, but the order-book names (Vertiv, grid) held their five-day gains: the market is selling AI spenders and crowded chips, not the power and cooling bottleneck.
regime: Nasdaq -2.9% and the semis ETF -7.0% on the day, with the semis ETF -14.2% and the Nasdaq -5.3% on the month; the VIX is 19.0. The 10-year is 4.93% and crude $99.41 (+9.1% on the month), so rates and oil still cap multiples. Software is the weakest group (-12.4% on five days, ServiceNow -33.9%) and investors are rotating out of AI into health care, financials and industrials (254f2e0524a1). Cooling (+1.8%) and grid (+4.9%) are positive on five days while compute (-4.0%) is not, so the split between suppliers with backlog and everyone else continues.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: Vertiv organic orders more than doubled, shares +19.7% on five days, Zacks Rank #1 (d8517aa55ef8, 23e7a19ac0c2)
Grid +4.9% and power +1.4% on five days while compute is -4.0% (digest segments)
Vistra bought 5.5GW of gas capacity to add supply (b81c30cab309); MasTec revenue +29.9% with a power-delivery backlog (e86e39401049)
Against: cooling and grid are still -15.5% and -10.7% on the month, and Hubbell and Trane fell on the week (digest segments)
theses.change_note: Five-day strength in grid and cooling against a weak tape supports the thesis, but one session adds no new fundamental evidence.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Amazon upgraded on 'strong demand visibility' to support aggressive capex (40a44185e8eb)
South Korea's October exports nearly doubled on semiconductor shipments (53c595df04a6)
Against: compute is -17.9% and foundry equipment -23.2% on the month; ETFs sold NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom and AMAT (24598603ab41, d6f21fcff3fa)
Against: Kioxia fell on a cautious memory outlook (0d29bdfe4cf0)
theses.change_note: -3: demand data is still strong, but the price action and ETF selling say the market no longer pays for it, and this thesis had no fresh company-level confirmation today.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: Nebius is down 36% on 'concerns about funding the AI build-out' (84ba0ab6ec1d)
IREN hit a 52-week low last week (b8f651c5ac8c)
Segment -25.4% on the month; the quality gate again dropped IREN, NBIS, CIFR, WULF, APLD and CRWV (shortlist)
Against: CoreWeave rose 7.9% on one day after locking in compute 'way under market' (ce035543cb2c)
theses.change_note: +1: funding-stress headlines continue and the gate drops the same names; CoreWeave's one-day bounce is the only counter.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Segment -25.1% on the month though Western Digital is +6.5% on five days (digest segments)
Western Digital profits are surging, yet one analyst doubts shares beat the June high by 2030 (61953bb8cb98)
Micron bounced on the market rebound with no catalyst while 'AI fears linger' (9b81d95b0940)
Against: Kioxia plunged on a cautious memory outlook (0d29bdfe4cf0)
theses.change_note: -4: Kioxia's cautious outlook is the first supplier-side crack in the shortage story, and the group lost another 8.5% in a day.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Alphabet's record $500B market-cap loss (6929405a7882); GOOGL -12.6% on five days (digest segments)
Dan Niles: Big Tech earnings were 'more trick than treat' and show AI risks (8a49b886f9e0)
Against: Phillip Securities upgraded Amazon on demand visibility and raised its target to $330 (40a44185e8eb)
Against: segment -2.5% on the day is the mildest of all groups (digest segments)
theses.change_note: -2: hyperscalers fell least today and Amazon got an upgrade; the cash-burn case is intact but the move is largely priced.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: 10-year 4.93%, crude $99.41, VIX +24.1% on the month (digest tape)
Tech had its worst month since March 2025; a firm modelled a 30% S&P drop (a11425d84ec4)
Investors are hedging against an AI downturn (4e0f5256680d); Morgan Stanley warns of a 9% S&P fall (4003e36f21a0)
Against: the 10-year is down 6.9% on the month and oil -4.5% on the day, so the rate leg is easing (digest tape)
theses.change_note: +5: semis -7.0% in a day, record hedging and rotation out of AI; the easing 10-year stops this going higher.

compute.note: -8.1% on the day and -17.9% on the month; Marvell -14.1% on five days, only Broadcom is up.

foundry_equipment.note: -23.2% on the month; KLA +8.5% on five days but Teradyne -11.2%; buy only quality (ASML, TSM).

memory_storage.note: Kioxia's cautious outlook and -25.1% on the month; cut from overweight until the supplier data steadies.

networking_optical.note: -21.2% on the month; Lumentum +11.2% on five days, fundamentals unchanged.

servers.note: -6.6% on the day; Dell -7.0% on five days; SMCI reports this week.

power_nuclear.note: Talen +4.6% on five days and Vistra adds 5.5GW; own cash-flow producers only, nuclear developers burn cash.

grid_electrical.note: +4.9% on five days led by Quanta (+13.6%); MasTec shows backlog with margin pressure.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv +19.7% on five days on doubled orders; Trane -7.8%; less margin of safety after the run.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Nebius -36% and IREN at lows on funding fears; fails the cash-flow gate.

hyperscalers.note: Capex outruns cash flow, though the group fell least today.

ai_software.note: -12.4% on five days with ServiceNow -33.9%; AI is a cost to them, not a tailwind.

risks: A second -7% semis day would show forced selling and could pull down the order-book names that held up.
Hyperscaler capex cuts after Big Tech earnings would hit every supplier despite strong backlogs.
Oil near $100 and a 10-year near 4.9% keep multiples compressed into the midterm elections.
Neocloud funding stress could cancel or delay GPU, power and cooling orders.
Sell-the-news on good prints means being right on fundamentals can still lose money.
watch: Apple earnings today on memory costs and the 'safe haven' test.
SMCI, AMD and Palantir earnings this week for server and AI demand.
BWXT (Nov 2) and Primoris (Nov 3) reports for nuclear and grid backlog.
Whether the semis ETF holds -14% on the month or breaks lower.
The 10-year against 5% and crude against $100, and the midterm elections.
